intro: The Brewers just put the NL on notice with a 20-0 demolition that clinched the division and stretched their lead to an embarrassing 10 games. Meanwhile, Texas pulled off the comeback of the year, erasing a 20-point deficit to snatch the No. 1 ranking from Ohio State in what's already being called an instant classic.

stories.headline: Brewers Clinch With a 20-0 Beatdown and a 10-Game Lead That's Getting Embarrassing
stories.body: Milwaukee clinched a playoff berth Friday by absolutely demolishing the Reds 20-0, because apparently a 10-game lead over the Cubs wasn't enough of a statement. The NL Central race is over — someone just forgot to tell the other four teams.

stories.headline: Cam Schlittler Throws One-Hit Gem, Takes MLB ERA Lead in Subway Series Finale
stories.body: Yankees rookie Cam Schlittler held the Mets to one hit over six innings Sunday, a 2-0 shutout win that pushed New York to the brink of a playoff berth and handed Schlittler the major league ERA lead. The Mets would like to forget this one existed.

stories.headline: White Sox Division Lead Down to Half a Game After Four Straight Losses
stories.body: Chicago's AL Central cushion has nearly evaporated, with Cleveland's 5-2 win in Minnesota tightening the race to a half-game margin after the Sox dropped their fourth straight. It's a great time for a four-game skid if you enjoy stress.

stories.headline: Texas Erases 20-Point Hole, Steals No. 1 from Ohio State in Instant Classic
stories.body: Down 23-3, No. 4 Texas outscored No. 1 Ohio State 21-0 in the final stretch to win 24-23 in the biggest moment of Steve Sarkisian's tenure in Austin. The Longhorns are now the new AP No. 1, and the Big Ten vs. SEC debate has a very loud new data point.

stories.headline: Oklahoma State Ends Its FBS Skid by Shellacking No. 6 Oregon
stories.body: Oklahoma State knocked off No. 6 Oregon 39-31 in one of the cleanest upsets of the young season, and it wasn't particularly close by the end. Week 2 was not kind to the Pac-12's surviving pride.

stories.headline: Michigan Quietly Beats Up Oklahoma While Everyone Watched Texas
stories.body: While the college football world was locked in on Austin, Michigan went out and beat No. 11 Oklahoma 17-10 to add another top-25 scalp to an already chaotic weekend. The AP poll reshuffled hard, and the playoff picture is already getting interesting six weeks before anyone expected.

stories.headline: Philly's Offense Is Already on Life Support: Brown and Dickerson Both Hit IR
stories.body: The Eagles are placing Pro Bowl guard Landon Dickerson and receiver A.J. Brown on injured reserve, costing them both players for at least the next four games. A knee injury and a high ankle sprain respectively — not exactly the start Philadelphia had in mind.

stories.headline: Tucker Kraft Gets Paid: Packers Lock Up Their TE on a $75M Deal
stories.body: Green Bay signed Tucker Kraft to a four-year, $75 million extension that can climb to $92 million with incentives, making him one of the highest-paid tight ends in the league. The Packers clearly aren't waiting to find out what he costs on the open market.

stories.headline: Garrett, Darnold, Murray: The NFL's Injury List Is Already a Mess
stories.body: Myles Garrett is headed for knee surgery with no return timetable, Sam Darnold has a mystery glute injury his team called a "very unique soft-tissue injury," and Kyler Murray is in the concussion protocol after Week 1. It's only September.

stories.headline: Rybakina Dethrones Sabalenka, Grabs No. 1 and Her First Flushing Meadows Crown
stories.body: Elena Rybakina beat Aryna Sabalenka in the US Open final to claim her third Grand Slam title and end Sabalenka's 99-week reign at world No. 1. Turns out the best way to stop a three-peat is to just beat the three-peater.

stories.headline: Zverev Makes It Two Slams in 2026, Shelton Finally Cracks a Major Final
stories.body: Alexander Zverev defeated Ben Shelton in four sets to win the US Open men's title, his second Grand Slam of the year, while Shelton's runner-up finish vaulted him to ATP No. 4. Zverev is having the kind of season that makes you wonder what took so long.

stories.headline: Alcaraz Bounced Early in What Became the Latest Match in US Open History
stories.body: Defending champion Carlos Alcaraz was eliminated before the final in a match reported as the latest-ever finish in US Open history, capping a tournament where his title defense quietly fell apart in the small hours. The night session giveth, and the night session taketh away.

stories.headline: Antonelli Makes It Eight: Kid From Mercedes Is Running Away With This Thing
stories.body: Kimi Antonelli won the Spanish Grand Prix in Madrid for his eighth victory of the season, stretching his championship lead over teammate George Russell to 81 points with just rounds remaining. Mercedes also leads the constructors' standings at 503 points, with Ferrari and McLaren not even close.

stories.headline: Norris Had It, Then a Virtual Safety Car Happened
stories.body: Lando Norris finished third in Madrid and said flat-out that he 'deserved' the win, but unlucky VSC timing handed the victory to Antonelli instead. Third place in a race you should have won is its own special kind of pain.

stories.headline: Hamilton Blanked, Leclerc and Lewis Bury the Hatchet After Monza
stories.body: Lewis Hamilton failed to score in Madrid, a rough weekend made slightly less bad by him and Charles Leclerc publicly declaring their Monza controversy 'squashed.' Ferrari is still 145 points behind Mercedes in the constructors' standings, so there are bigger problems than teammate drama anyway.

stories.headline: Como Walk Into the Champions League and Immediately Embarrass RB Leipzig
stories.body: Italian newcomers Como thrashed Bundesliga side RB Leipzig 4–1 in their very first Champions League match, with manager Cesc Fàbregas declaring his side lived up to the competition's standards. Bold words — somehow completely earned.

stories.headline: Arsenal Still Perfect, Liverpool and Chelsea Already Dropping Points
stories.body: Arsenal made it 12 points from 12 with a 2–0 win at Sunderland, while title rivals Liverpool and Chelsea were both held to draws in the same Premier League round. Four games in and the gap is already doing some talking.

stories.headline: Haaland Wants Barcelona, Mac Allister Might Leave Liverpool — Rumor Mill Is Spinning
stories.body: Spanish outlet El Nacional reports Erling Haaland is keen on a €175m move to Barcelona, while Fabrizio Romano says Alexis Mac Allister could walk out of Liverpool next year without a new deal. Neither is done, but neither is nothing.

stories.headline: Clippers Get Nuked: $30M Fine, Ballmer Banned, Five Picks Gone — and Now the DOJ Is Involved
stories.body: The NBA hammered the Clippers with a $30 million fine, a one-year suspension for Steve Ballmer, and five forfeited first-round picks over salary-cap circumvention tied to the Kawhi Leonard situation. The U.S. Department of Justice has now opened a criminal probe, which is a sentence no franchise ever wants written about them.

stories.headline: Kawhi's Going Back to Toronto — Raptors Land Leonard for Ingram, Dick, and a Haul of Picks
stories.body: With the Clippers saga forcing the deal forward, Shams Charania reports the teams have agreed on a trade sending Kawhi Leonard back to Toronto in exchange for Brandon Ingram, Gradey Dick, two first-round picks, one pick swap, and two second-round picks. The Raptors are getting their guy back; the Clippers are getting a rebuild they very much did not plan for.

stories.headline: Mark Williams Out Long-Term After Shoulder Surgery
stories.body: Mark Williams underwent surgery to repair a torn labrum in his left shoulder and is expected to miss an extended period. Rough timing for a big man still working to establish himself in the league.

stories.headline: Zach Johnson Birdies His Way to No. 5 on Tour Champions
stories.body: Johnson closed with back-to-back birdies to edge Ben Crane by one shot at the Sanford International, finishing 11-under and notching his fifth win of the season. That ties him with Stewart Cink for the most wins on PGA Tour Champions this year — not bad for a guy who needed a clutch finish just to get there.

stories.headline: Alvaro Ortiz Runs Away With Simmons Bank Open, Books PGA Tour Ticket
stories.body: Ortiz fired a closing 63 to win the Simmons Bank Open by four shots at 26-under, locking up his PGA Tour card for 2027 in the process. Sandy Scott hung around through 54 holes but couldn't keep up on Sunday — story of the week.

stories.headline: Papineau Turns 30 With a 61 and a Trophy
stories.body: Étienne Papineau shot a final-round 61 on his 30th birthday to win the Digital Commerce Group Open by four strokes and claim his second PGA Tour Americas title of 2026. He also jumped to No. 2 on the points list, which is a pretty solid birthday present.

stories.headline: Bedard Gets the 'C' — Blackhawks Make It Official
stories.body: Connor Bedard has been named the 37th captain in Chicago Blackhawks history, making him one of the youngest players ever to wear the 'C' for the franchise. No pressure, kid — just carry a century-old organization on your shoulders.

stories.headline: Batherson Cashes In: Ottawa Drops $86M on Their Guy
stories.body: Drake Batherson re-signed with the Senators on an eight-year, $86 million deal — the largest contract in franchise history — complete with $30 million in signing bonuses and a full no-move clause for the first four years. Ottawa is betting big on keeping their core together, which is either a great sign or a very expensive leap of faith.

stories.headline: Detroit in Chaos: No Captain, New Interim GM
stories.body: The Red Wings are heading into the season without a captain after Dylan Larkin's leadership situation fell apart, and Shawn Horcoff has been named interim GM as Detroit continues a broader front-office search. It's a lot of 'interim' energy for a franchise that really needs some answers.
